keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1340-1343, before Cliopatria's first shape. 'Despite all loss Hasan Buzurg retained control of Diyar Bakr, Iraq, Khuzestan and Baghdad' after the peace of late 1338 (when he lost Azerbaijan to Hasan Kuchak); 'After he stopped recognizing Togha in 1344, he still did not proclaim himself independent', which is probably why Cliopatria begins in 1344. The 1344 shape is used for these years. fx-13 (F317, F152): the Cliopatria outline holds the whole of Lorestan province (121 cells, Khorramabad) and, in Khuzestan, the Idaj district and the Bakhtiari country (28 and 16 cells), which are the Khorshidi and Hazaraspid lands. Khorshidi page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khorshidi_dynasty): capital Khorramabad; the only Jalayirid mention is the 1383 marriage of one of Izz al-Din's daughters to Ahmad bin Uways Jalayir, when the Muzaffarid Shah Shoja 'visited Khorramabad with his army'; Timur's raids 1386-1393; 'In 1395-96, Muhammad Sultan, governor of Fars, extended his authority over all of Luristan and Khuzestan'; no overlordship of the Jalayirids is stated. Hazaraspids page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hazaraspids): the capital Idaj is 'located in present-day northern Khuzestan', the dynasty ruled mainly in Lorestan, and in Pashang's reign (1355-1378) it 'faced attacks from the Muzaffarids' when Idaj 'temporarily fell into their hands'. The Jalayirid Sultanate and Hasan Buzurg pages name neither Lorestan nor the Hazaraspids, so Lorestan, the Bakhtiari country and the Idaj district (60 km) are cut out (confidence 1-2). The rest of Khuzestan stays: the Hasan Buzurg page has him keep 'Diyar Bakr, Iraq, Khuzestan and Baghdad' after the late-1338 peace (the sentence follows 'Peace was declared in late 1338'). The Hazaraspids claim the same plain: their page has Yusuf Shah I (r. 1274-1288) 'added Khuzestan' and Yusuf Shah II (r. 1330-1340) 'annexed the cities of Shushtar, Hoveizeh and Basra'. No page dates an end to either claim, so both stay drawn and the size rule gives the 177 cells of the Khuzestan plain to the Hazaraspids (the smaller state); nothing is asked of the hazaraspids dossier.

1357: the Jalayirids occupy Tiflis. 'The Jalayirids then occupied Tiflis in 1357-1358', after the Golden Horde overran the Chobanids; hatched, not annexed.
1358: Tiflis is left (the occupation lasted 1357-1358).
1358: the seat moves to Tabriz (infobox 'Tabriz (1358-1388)'; the page's text has Uways take Tabriz in 1360).
August 1358: Uways conquers Azerbaijan from the Golden Horde. Azerbaijan 'overrun by the forces of the Golden Horde under Jani Beg in 1357'; 'Uvais conquered the area in August 1358'.
1359: the Muzaffarid Shah Shuja takes Tabriz. 'Shah Shoja (Muzaffarid) occupied Azerbaijan and Arran for four months and briefly captured Tabriz'.
1360: Uways retakes Azerbaijan. 'Uways reconquered Azerbaijan with its capital, Tabriz' (the Awais page: 'Uways was now master of Azerbaijan once again').

1364: Uways campaigns against Shirvan. 'In 1364, Shaykh Uways Jalayir campaigned against the Shirvanshah Kavus. Later, his emir Bayram Beg besieged Shamakhi, and Kavus became a Jalayirid vassal.' The vassalage is undated ('later'); 1364 is the campaign.
1374: Uways dies at Tabriz (10 October 1374). The page is silent on Shirvan afterwards; the end of the relation is bridged to his death.
1384: Timur takes Soltaniyeh. 'Timur attacked and took Soltaniyeh.'
1386: Timur takes Tabriz and Azerbaijan. 'Timur captured Tabriz, and Azerbaijan stayed under Timurid control'; in 1392 Timur entrusted Azerbaijan to Miran Shah.
1388: the seat returns to Baghdad (infobox 'Baghdad (1388-1411)'; the text has Ahmad based in Baghdad from 1386).

region.text: Baghdad and the Jalayirid core in Iraq

ledger.note: 1393: Timur captures Baghdad and Ahmad flees to the Mamluks. 'Timur captured Baghdad, and Ahmad fled to the Mamluks.'

region.text: Baghdad and the Jalayirid core in Iraq

ledger.note: 1394: Ahmad retakes Baghdad. 'With Mamluk support, Ahmad recaptured Baghdad' (the Sarbadars page: 'forced to retreat in 1394 when Sultan Ahmad of the Jalayirids marched to recapture the city').

region.text: Baghdad and the Jalayirid core in Iraq

ledger.note: 1401: Timur takes Baghdad after a forty-day siege. 'Timur besieged the Jalayirid Sultanate capital of Baghdad for forty days'; infobox 'Timurid occupation of Baghdad (1401-1405)'; the Jalayirid page: 'Ahmad abandoned Baghdad, and Timur took it'. No month on either page.

1405: Ahmad recovers Baghdad after Timur's death. 'When Timur died in 1405 Nasir-ad-Din Faraj released Sultan Ahmad Jalayir and Qara Yusuf'; Ahmad, 'taking advantage of a local insurrection, finally managed to recapture the city of Baghdad' (no month). The page dates Timur's death and Ahmad's release to 1405 but gives no year for the recapture itself (confidence lowered from 3 to 2 by the me-09-g reviewer, 2026-10-25).

1406: Tabriz passes to Ahmad. Qara Yusuf took Tabriz after the 'Battle of Nakhchivan (1406)'; Ahmad then 'occupied Tabriz when Qara Yusuf was away in Armenia', and 'After expelling Qara Yusuf from Tabriz, Ahmad Jalayir would hold residence there between 1406 and 1410' (Jalayirid page, no month). (Counterpart corrected from timurid-empire to qara-qoyunlu and the unsupported month October dropped by the me-09-g reviewer, 2026-10-25.)
1409: the seat moves to Hillah (infobox 'Hillah (1409-1410)').
1410: Qara Yusuf kills Ahmad and takes Tabriz. 'Qara Yusuf killed Ahmad' after 'Ahmad held Tabriz from 1406 to 1410'; Qara Yusuf had entered Tabriz in the fall of 1409.
1410: Baghdad is lost and the dynasty is 'pushed into lower Iraq (Hillah, Wasit, Basra)'. The page gives no separate date for Baghdad.
1411: the seat moves to Basra (infobox 'Basra (1411-1432)').

1423: Sultan Muhammad is expelled from Shushtar by the Timurids. The Jalayirid page: in 1423 the penultimate ruler 'was expelled from Shushtar by the Timurid Governor of Fars Ibrahim Sultan'. (Counterpart corrected from 'Ibrahim Sultan' to timurid-empire by the me-09-g reviewer, 2026-10-25.)
October 1431: the Qara Qoyunlu take Hillah. 'The Qara Qoyunlu captured al-Hella in October.'

region.text: lower Iraq: Hillah, Wasit and Basra

ledger.note: 1432: the Qara Qoyunlu end the Jalayirids. 'The Jalayirids were finally eliminated by the Qara Qoyunlu in 1432' (the same page has Hosayn killed on 9 November 1431).

wars.name: Chobanid attack on Baghdad (1347)
wars.outcome: The Chobanid army sent by Malik Ashraf failed to take Baghdad: 'Jalayirid forces, however, inflicted heavy losses on the force, which was forced to retreat by the summer.'
wars.note: No ground changed hands, so no contested zone.

wars.name: Golden Horde conquest of Azerbaijan
wars.outcome: Jani Beg's Golden Horde overran the Chobanids in 1357 (Tabriz taken, Malik Ashraf executed); Uways conquered Azerbaijan in August 1358.
wars.note: The Golden Horde dossier dates Jani Beg's capture of Tabriz to 1356, the Chobanids page to 1357.

wars.name: Muzaffarid occupation of Azerbaijan
wars.outcome: Shah Shuja held Azerbaijan, Arran and briefly Tabriz for four months in 1359; Uways reconquered it in 1360.

wars.name: Jalayirid campaigns against Shirvan and the Qara Qoyunlu
wars.outcome: The Shirvanshah Kavus became a Jalayirid vassal after Bayram Beg besieged Shamakhi; in 1366 Uways defeated Birdi Khwaja of the Black Sheep Turkmen.
wars.note: The Awais page places the 1366 victory at Mosul, the Jalayirid page at Mush; neither changes a frontier.

wars.name: Timur's wars against the Jalayirids
wars.outcome: Timur took Soltaniyeh (1384), Tabriz (1386), Baghdad (1393, lost again 1394) and Baghdad again in 1401; Ahmad took refuge with the Mamluks.

wars.name: Siege of Baghdad (1401)
wars.outcome: Timur besieged Baghdad for forty days; Ahmad fled; Baghdad stayed under Timurid occupation until 1405.

wars.name: Qara Qoyunlu conquest of the Jalayirid lands

zones.text: lower Iraq: Hillah, Wasit and Basra

wars.outcome: Qara Yusuf retook Tabriz in 1406 jointly with Ahmad, killed him in 1410 and pushed the dynasty into lower Iraq; Hillah fell in October 1431 and the Jalayirids ended in 1432.
wars.note: The page's 1431/1432 end dates conflict (Hosayn killed 9 November 1431).

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is given by any page opened; Iraq's river frontiers and the Azerbaijan and Zagros marches are approximate, and the dynasty's holdings change by raid, siege and succession.

notes: Pages: five (budget 5). Start year: the Jalayirid page gives 1340 (text) and 1336 (rulers table); the Hasan Buzurg page gives the late-1338 peace that left him Iraq, Khuzestan, Diyar Bakr and Baghdad and 1344 as the year he stopped recognizing Togha Temur; this dossier uses 1340 and the 1344 Cliopatria shape for 1340-1343. End year: Cliopatria ends the row in 1401 (Timur's capture of Baghdad) but the dynasty ruled Tabriz 1406-1410 and lower Iraq to 1432 (page); 1402-1404 the state is landless (Ahmad in Mamluk captivity), so there is no keyframe for those years. Cliopatria's relation '(Allegiance of Jalayirid Sultanate to Timurid Empire)' 1375-1394 is not supported by any page opened: the Jalayirid page shows Timur attacking in 1384, 1386 and 1393, and the sentence 'Uways first recognized the sovereignty of the Blue Horde' is the only vassalage on the page. Cliopatria rows that conflict with this dossier: the Chobanids shape runs to 1362 and still covers Azerbaijan though the Chobanids ended in 1357; the Qara Qoyunlu shape covers Azerbaijan from 1375 and the Timurid Empire shape covers it in 1410, while the Jalayirid page has Jalayirid Tabriz until 1386 and 1406-1410; the Golden Horde dossier dates Jani Beg's Tabriz to 1356. Capital years follow the infobox (Tabriz 1358-1388) though the text dates Uways's Tabriz to 1360. Unverified: Mosul (in the 1363 shape, outside the 1375 shape; no page dates a loss), Khuzestan between 1395 and 1423, and the Shirvan vassalage dates (1364 campaign and 1374 are bridging, confidence 1). Gazetteer names used: none missing (Soltaniyeh, Shushtar, Wasit, Al Hillah are places; Wasit also admin1). Counterpart 'Ibrahim Sultan' (1423) is a person named by the page, whose state the page does not name.
